project_context.title: HamClock Next — SDL2 Rewrite
project_context.origin: This project is a full rewrite of Elwood Downey (WB0OEW)'s HamClock, a feature-rich amateur radio dashboard originally targeting ESP32 and Raspberry Pi via a custom framebuffer/X11 rendering stack. Elwood became a Silent Key on 29 January 2026. This rewrite is dedicated to his memory.
project_context.why_rewrite: The original codebase accumulated ~1.2 million lines across monolithic files (setup.cpp alone is 207K). Incremental patching was unsustainable. The rewrite adopts SDL2, separates concerns into widget classes, uses libcurl/libpredict instead of custom protocol stacks, and targets any SDL2-capable desktop or embedded Linux system.
philosophy: Each feature is a self-contained Widget class with a consistent interface.
Data fetching is separated from rendering: every widget has a *Provider (services/) and a *Panel (ui/).
Core data structures live in src/core/ as plain data types.
The layout is fluid/responsive — not hardcoded to 800x480 like the original.
SDL2 RGBA replaces RGB565. SDL_ttf replaces all custom font/segment renderers.
libpredict v2 replaces Plan 13 for satellite orbit propagation.
libcurl with ETag/Last-Modified caching replaces the custom WiFi/HTTP stack.
JSON config replaces NVRAM and ESP32-specific storage.

tech_stack.config: JSON file on disk via ConfigManager
tech_stack.web_api: Embedded HTTP server (src/network/WebServer), documented in API.md

source_layout.description: Directory structure of the hamclock-next codebase. Every directory has a clear single responsibility.

tree.src/main.cpp: Entry point. Initializes SDL2, ConfigManager, WebServer, then enters the main event/render loop.
tree.src/core/: Pure data types, store classes, and shared utilities. No SDL or network calls here.
tree.src/ui/: All Widget/Panel classes. Each file is a self-contained renderable unit.
tree.src/services/: Data providers. Each provider fetches and caches data for one domain.

naming_conventions.widget_pair: Every panel that displays data has a {Name}Panel.cpp/.h (rendering) paired with a {Name}Provider.cpp/.h (data).
naming_conventions.data_struct: Data structures live in src/core/ as {Name}Data.h or {Name}Store.h.
naming_conventions.infrastructure: Singleton-style managers: ConfigManager, NetworkManager, WebServer, UIRegistry.
naming_conventions.original_vs_next: Original used flat .cpp files with global functions. Next uses classes. Example: original updateDXCluster() global → next DXClusterProvider::update() + DXClusterPanel::render().

widget_scaffolding.description: The fastest way to add a new widget or complete a partial one. Follow these steps and fill in the domain-specific logic.
steps: 1. Create src/core/{Name}Data.h — plain struct with the data fields the widget displays.
2. Create src/services/{Name}Provider.h/.cpp — fetches data via NetworkManager, stores in {Name}Data.
3. Create src/ui/{Name}Panel.h/.cpp — renders the data using SDL2. Inherits or follows the Widget interface.
4. Register the widget in src/core/WidgetType.h and src/core/UIRegistry.h.
5. If the widget exposes map overlays, integrate with MapWidget::render().
6. Add REST endpoints to WebServer if needed (follow API.md conventions).
7. Update feature_map.json status from 'partial'/'missing' to 'implemented' when acceptance criteria are met.
important_notes: NetworkManager handles HTTP. Call NetworkManager::instance().get(url) — it returns cached data when ETag/Last-Modified hasn't changed.
ConfigManager::instance().getConfig() for reading/modifying settings. ConfigManager::instance().save(cfg) to persist.
Theme.h has all color constants. Use getThemeColors(theme_) to obtain a ThemeColors struct — never hardcode SDL_Color values.
Standardize all setup/confirmation buttons: Use 'Done' and 'Cancel' labels (PascalCase).
Standard button sizes: 100x34 for main modals, 80x28 for small widget-based setups.
FontManager handles scaled TTF fonts. Never load your own TTF file.
SDL coordinates: (0,0) is top-left. x_/y_ is the panel's top-left corner.
All render() calls happen on the main thread. Providers run on a background thread. Use a mutex or std::atomic if sharing state.
The WebServer debug endpoint /debug/widgets calls getDebugData() on all registered panels — always implement it.
If a provider uses NetworkManager::fetchAsync, it MUST inherit from std::enable_shared_from_this and capture a weak_ptr in the lambda to prevent use-after-free crashes during configuration reloads.

If a provider's API may be unavailable or require auth, add a `bool fetched` flag to the data struct (default false). The provider pushes event on completion with `fetched=true, valid=false` on error — panel shows meaningful status (e.g. 'API key required') rather than indefinite 'Loading...' state.
Widget::onMouseDown(int mx, int my, Uint16 mod) added for advanced interactivity (Phase 60).
Widget::onMouseUp now takes `int clicks` as 4th parameter (Uint16 mod, int clicks). Update all Widget subclasses when overriding.
- COLORS: Never hardcode `SDL_Color{r,g,b,a}`. Always use `getThemeColors(theme_)` to obtain `ThemeColors` tokens (success, danger, warning, accent, text, textDim).
- GRAPHS: Plots must use anti-aliased textures. Use `RenderUtils::drawPolylineTextured` with the 'line_aa' texture. Avoid raw `SDL_RenderDrawLine` for data plots.
- TOOLTIPS: All interactive graphs must implement `onMouseMove` tooltips. Use the base `renderTooltip` (standardized in Widget.h) to ensure consistent theme-adaptive appearance.
- FONTS: Use the `FontCatalog` (via `cat->drawText`) with `FontStyle` tokens. Avoid raw `TTF_Font` manipulation in panels.

original_vs_next.description: Key architectural differences between Elwood's original and hamclock-next. Essential context for anyone touching both codebases.

differences.original: Custom framebuffer abstraction + X11/EGL/ESP32 display HAL. RGB565 color format.
differences.next: SDL2 with full RGBA. SDL_ttf for fonts, SDL_image for textures. Runs anywhere SDL2 runs.

differences.original: Flat directory of .cpp files, many 30K–207K lines. Global functions, global state.
differences.next: Layered: core/ → services/ → ui/ → network/. Class-per-widget. No globals except singletons.

differences.original: Custom seven-segment renderer (sevenseg.cpp), custom font bitmaps.
differences.next: SDL_ttf with FontManager. seven_segment feature is not_needed — TTF fonts cover all cases.

differences.original: Plan 13 orbital propagation (P13.cpp). P13 is a classic algorithm from 1983.
differences.next: libpredict v2 (modern successor to P13). Same math, cleaner API, actively maintained.

differences.original: NVRAM abstraction (nvram.cpp) — maps to ESP32 Preferences or flat file. setup.cpp is 207K.
differences.next: JSON file via ConfigManager. setup.cpp equivalent is SetupScreen.cpp — a fraction of the size.

differences.original: wifi.cpp (78K) — custom HTTP stack, WiFi management for ESP32, connection pooling.
differences.next: libcurl via NetworkManager. ETag/Last-Modified caching built in. libcurl handles TLS, redirects, timeouts.
WebServer.cpp — lean, documented REST API. Endpoints registered per-feature.

differences.original: Hardcoded 800x480 (ESP32 display size). Pixel positions are magic numbers throughout.
differences.next: LayoutManager + PaneContainer. Responsive. Widgets get a setBounds(SDL_Rect) call.

differences.original: I2C BME280, CPU temp via sysfs, GPIO brightness PWM, GPS NMEA, OTA firmware update.
differences.next: Desktop-first. Hardware features (BME280, GPS, brightness PWM, OTA) are missing — low priority unless RPi-specific build target is added.

differences.original: Azimuthal equidistant (primary), Robinson, Mercator, sphere projection.
differences.next: Azimuthal equidistant (Phase 26: high-fidelity with NASA Black Marble night lights). Robinson (v0.7B) and Mercator (v0.8B) projections implemented and selectable via MapViewMenu.

implemented_features.notes: AlertBadge struct added to SpaceWeatherPanel. Blinking G/R/S badge at 1 Hz when any NOAA scale ≥ 3.

implemented_features.notes: Polls GitHub Releases API; cached 6h. Robust version comparison (dots/v-prefix, internal vs release format, numeric segment + beta suffix). TimePanel version string turns amber + appends * when update available. UpdateOverlay: 760x440px, Markdown rendering (H1/H2/H3, bullet lists), Skip/Not Now/Update result enum. implemented_features.notes: FrameCapture: SDL renderer → JPEG frames. /stream.mjpeg MJPEG endpoint. /live MJPEG viewer page. setMaxFps(30) in headless mode.

implemented_features.notes: --live-web CLI flag; auto-detects headless (offscreen SDL driver or /.dockerenv). Interactive canvas viewer with aspect-ratio scaling, R/W R/O badge, pointer/touch/keyboard injection, reconnect on stream error. Endpoints: /live/touch, /live/key, /live/mouse, /live/status (403 when disabled). All guarded by #ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__.

implemented_features.notes: /api/config GET returns 30+ AppConfig fields (qrzPassword write-only). /set_config extended with 25 new params (DX Cluster, Rig, Rotator, QRZ, Live Spots, Brightness, GPS/RSS/ONTA toggles). 4 new browser config tabs: Cluster, Radio, Services, Brightness. Routes moved outside #ifdef ENABLE_DEBUG_API (fixes 404s in default builds).

implemented_features.name: Graph Hover Tooltips & AA Lines
implemented_features.notes: Shared Tooltip infrastructure in base Widget class. Hover tooltips on Aurora, Dst, History (solar flux/SSN/Kp) panels. 2px AA lines with Gaussian falloff. PaneContainer mouse motion event forwarding fixed. Procedural texture generation for line_aa and circular markers in main.cpp.

implemented_features.notes: HubMode enum (Off/Master/Client) in AppConfig. Master exposes /api/hub/fetch (base64-encoded target URL, max_age param). SetupScreen Network tab: mode cycle button + conditional IP/Port fields for Client mode. Config persists in hub.{mode,ip,port} JSON section.

for_new_contributors: Read this MCP and the API.md in the repo root before touching any code.
Check missing_features for remaining deferred work (bme280_sensor only — all map projections now implemented). All other features are implemented.
Follow the widget_scaffolding steps. Do not deviate from the Provider/Panel/Data naming pattern.
Use Theme:: color constants. Use FontManager for text. Never hardcode pixel positions — use _bounds from setBounds().
Implement getDebugData() in every Panel — it feeds /debug/widgets and is essential for remote debugging.
When a feature is complete, update feature_map.json: change status to 'implemented', verify acceptance criteria.
Test with the WebServer: /live.jpg shows the current state, /debug/widgets shows widget health.
for_ai_assistants: This project uses C++20. Use modern C++ idioms: auto, range-for, std::optional, std::variant, structured bindings, if constexpr where appropriate.
Do not suggest ESP32-specific code. This is a desktop/embedded Linux SDL2 application.
When implementing a partial feature, check what already exists in the listed next_files before writing new code.
The original codebase (master branch) is reference material for behavior, NOT for code style or architecture.
libpredict v2 docs: https://github.com/la1k/libpredict — use for all satellite tracking math.
libcurl is already integrated via NetworkManager. Do not add new HTTP libraries.
SDL2 docs: https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2 — SDL_Renderer, SDL_Texture, SDL_ttf, SDL_image are all in use.
When unsure about an API endpoint format, check API.md and follow the existing pattern in WebServer.cpp.
feature_map.json is the source of truth for what is done, partial, or missing. Update it when you complete work.
code_style: 2-space indentation (spaces, not tabs — actual codebase convention).
Braces on same line for control flow, own line for class/function definitions.
Class members with TRAILING underscore: x_, y_, width_, height_, data_, nextFetch_. NOT leading underscore.
Public API first in header, private last.
No raw owning pointers — use std::unique_ptr or std::shared_ptr.
Colors: always use ThemeColors struct from getThemeColors(theme_) — never hardcode SDL_Color{r,g,b,a} in widget render paths.
Windows portability: no localtime_r without #ifdef _WIN32 guard; no raw POSIX sockets — use DXClusterProvider.cpp as reference.

phase_37.name: Raspberry Pi Memory Optimization & Segfault Prevention
phase_37.summary: Resolved critical 'Cannot allocate memory' errors and subsequent segfaults on Raspberry Pi KMSDRM backend through tooltip texture caching, robust NULL checks, and low-memory rendering modes.
phase_37.problem: Frequent texture allocation/deallocation (180 creates per 3 seconds for tooltips) exhausted DRM descriptor pool on RPi. Unchecked NULL pointers cascaded into segfaults. Heavy SDL_RenderGeometry usage (96×48 grids = 4608 vertices) triggered internal buffer reallocations.
solutions: Tooltip texture caching: Textures now cached per tooltip text, only regenerated on text change (99% reduction: 180→1-2 allocations)
Robust NULL checks: Added checks after all SDL_CreateTexture, fontMgr_.renderText(), and texMgr_.get() calls with SDL_GetError() logging
Low-memory mode: Automatic 75% mesh density reduction for KMSDRM (96×48→48×24 grids for night overlay and Robinson projection)
Reduced geometry complexity: Great circle paths 250→100 segments, satellite footprint 72→36 segments
Enhanced diagnostics: SDL_GetError() messages with context (surface dimensions, texture keys, byte counts)

display_power_architecture.description: DisplayPower — KMSDRM + SDL2 Blanking Architecture (RPi3B verified 2026-03-09)
display_power_architecture.root_cause: On RPi3B with KMSDRM, SDL2 owns the display pipeline. While SDL2 is actively calling SDL_RenderPresent(), no external blanking command (fbdev FBIOBLANK, vcgencmd display_power) can cut the HDMI signal — they blank visually but the monitor never enters power-saving mode and shows no HDMI input label on wake.
display_power_architecture.solution: One-shot black frame pattern: (1) setPower(false) sets needsBlackFrame_=true, (2) consumeBlackFrame() returns true once (next render tick), (3) render loop: if consumeBlackFrame() → SDL_RenderPresent() once to clear screen, (4) subsequent ticks: getPower()==false → return without SDL_RenderPresent, (5) with no new frames, KMSDRM DPMS idle timer can engage → true power-off.

voacap_overlays.decision: VOACAP world map overlays (MUF/REL/TOA) are the highest-priority parity gap. The open-hamclock-backend already has a complete physics engine (voacap_service.py with NumPy vectorization). The decision is to proxy to OHB rather than port the Python/NumPy physics to C++.
voacap_overlays.rationale: voacap_service.py is 722 lines of complex ionospheric physics with NumPy vectorization. Porting to C++ would be months of work and risk introducing bugs in the physics model. OHB is already in the repo. The proxy approach lets us ship parity quickly while leaving the C++ port as a future optimization.
implementation_path: 1. Add fetchVOACAP-MUF.pl and fetchVOACAP-TOA.pl to open-hamclock-backend (they call voacap_service.py which is already there)
2. Create src/services/VoacapProvider.cpp that fetches from /api/propagation/voacap → overlay_endpoint
3. Add SDL_Texture overlay blending in MapWidget (pattern: same as DX Cluster spots, but full-image texture)
voacap_overlays.backend_free_path: KC2G MUF-RT only — fetch https://prop.kc2g.com/renders/current/mufd-normal-now.png. No frequency/mode params. Covers the most common use case (current MUF conditions).
voacap_overlays.reprojection_note: Overlay is 660x330 equirectangular. MapWidget uses azimuthal equidistant. MVP: render overlay in flat projection panel. Full parity: reproject 660x330 grid pixels to azimuthal coordinates in MapWidget::render() using the inverse of screenToLatLon().

propagation_overlay_alignment.issue: VOACAP overlays from open-hamclock-backend are 660x330 equirectangular (lat/lon grid). MapWidget's default view is azimuthal equidistant centered on DE. These projections do not align — you cannot simply blit the overlay PNG onto the map.
propagation_overlay_alignment.solution_mvp: Show the overlay in a separate flat-map panel (e.g., a secondary MapWidget or a dedicated OverlayPanel with equirectangular rendering). The original HamClock also had two map modes — 'map A' (azimuthal) and 'map B' (flat). Implement a similar switch.
propagation_overlay_alignment.solution_full: Re-project the 660x330 pixel grid: for each screen pixel in MapWidget, compute its lat/lon via screenToLatLon(), look up the corresponding pixel in the equirectangular overlay, and blend. This is O(screen_w * screen_h) per frame but can be done once when the overlay updates (every 30 min).
propagation_overlay_alignment.wasm_note: In WASM mode, the KC2G MUF-RT PNG is fetched via the CORS proxy (/proxy/https://prop.kc2g.com/renders/current/mufd-normal-now.png). Ensure serve.py or the nginx cors-proxy.conf proxies that URL pattern.
